details: Recent US inflation data, including a 6% year-over-year surge in the Producer Price Index (PPI) and a 3.8% rise in the Consumer Price Index (CPI), has intensified concerns about persistent inflation. This strengthens the "higher-for-longer" interest rate narrative, making non-yielding assets like Bitcoin less attractive and contributing to its fall below the $80,000 mark.
title: US Inflation Fuels Rate Fears, Bitcoin Drops Below $80K

details: Bank of England Deputy Governor Sarah Breeden indicated that the central bank is re-evaluating its proposed rules for stablecoins, which had drawn criticism from the industry. The initial proposals included requiring issuers to hold 40% of backing assets as unremunerated deposits and implementing holding caps for individuals and businesses. The BoE is now open to alternative regulatory approaches to achieve its stability objectives.
title: Bank of England Reconsiders Strict Stablecoin Rules

details: ECB President Christine Lagarde expressed reservations about privately issued stablecoins, citing their vulnerability to market stress and potential to draw deposits away from traditional banks. She advocated for Europe to promote euro-denominated digital instruments. Concurrently, the ECB is supporting the integrated development of DLT-based financial markets through initiatives like "Pontes" and "Appia" for tokenized assets.
title: ECB Cautious on Private Stablecoins, Supports DLT in Finance

details: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) published a paper asserting that tokenization represents a fundamental restructuring of financial architecture rather than just a technological enhancement. The IMF emphasized the critical need for clear policy frameworks, safe settlement assets, robust governance, legal certainty, and international coordination to manage new systemic vulnerabilities introduced by tokenization and ensure financial stability.
title: IMF Declares Tokenization a Structural Shift, Urges Policy Action

details: US retail sales in April grew by a slower-than-expected 0.5%, falling short of March's 1.6% gain. Concurrently, initial jobless claims for the week ending May 9th increased to 211,000, surpassing forecasts. These mixed economic signals, coupled with persistent inflation, contribute to uncertainty regarding future interest rate policies and the broader economic outlook.
title: US Retail Sales Slow, Jobless Claims Rise Amid Inflation
